summary: You spend each round guessing which of two role cards (or seven, at the highest complexity) opponents will pick, since everyone secretly chooses a phase and you benefit only from phases you also chose. It plays fast and silent for a card game, with almost no table talk, as engines of tableau-built worlds and developments snowball into big scoring turns.
praised: Extremely tight, elegant engine-building with dense, meaningful card text
High replayability from card variety and multiple viable strategies
Fast turns once players know the icons, giving a lot of depth per minute of playtime
Strong solo mode and satisfying multiplayer solitaire-with-a-twist puzzle
criticised: Steep learning curve and iconography that intimidates new players
Low direct interaction feels like parallel solitaire to some groups
Military/conflict subtheme is thin and abstract compared to the economic engine
Card draw and starting hand can swing outcomes before skill takes over

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with phase-selection bluffing

scoring.why: Winners combine tableau VP from played cards, chip VP from consuming goods, and end-game bonuses, so efficient engine synergy across several scoring sources decides it
